title: "LFP Compression Benchmark: SVD and Adaptive SVD+WP Methods"
description: "Benchmarking SVD-based LFP compression methods on 11 Neuropixels insertions, evaluating RMSE and SNR across compression ratios up to 3000×."
date: "2026-06-09"
author: "Olivier Winter"
categories: [electrophysiology, LFP, compression, Neuropixels]
---

## Overview

The IBL holds **936 hours** of Brainwide Map (BWM) recordings and **1472 hours** from the Ephys Atlas.
Raw LFP at 2500 Hz, 384 channels, float32 amounts to ~12 TB for the BWM alone.
After standard preprocessing (bad-channel rejection, 2–250 Hz bandpass, ×10 decimation to 250 Hz), the footprint shrinks to ~1.2 Tb — still too large for routine distribution or streaming.
The goal is to identify a lossy compression strategy that reduces this further.

**Practical recommendation: SVD + WP (ε≈150, α≈28) gives total CR≈125 (104-181) with RMSE≈15 µV and SNR≈10 dB.**
**This would shrink the 936-hour BWM dataset to ~9.6 Gb.**


## Pre-processing pipeline

Raw LFP (NP1, 2500 Hz, `.cbin`) was preprocessed before benchmarking:

1. **Bad-channel detection** — channels with anomalous variance flagged and excluded.
2. **Bandpass + CAR + decimation** — 2–250 Hz FIR bandpass, common-average referencing, ×10 FIR decimation → 250 Hz float32.
3. **Cadzow PPCA spatial denoising** — F-X Cadzow on 3 s snippets (nw=64, f_max=100 Hz, max rank r=5, adaptive rank via singular-value gap threshold=2.0, PPCA outlier k=2.0) to remove incoherent channel noise.

All methods were benchmarked on the Cadzow-denoised snippets so residuals reflect compression loss, not pre-existing noise.

![Cadzow denoising for PID e8f9fba4. Three 3 s snippets (rows): original / denoised (adaptive rank) / difference (same colour scale).](figures/2026-06-06_cadzow_e8f9fba4-d151-4b00-bee7-447f0f3e752c.png)

## Compression methods

| Method | Principle | CR formula | Parameters |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SVD-adapt** | First-stage: truncated SVD with adaptive rank: retain components where $s_k > \varepsilon \cdot \sigma_0$, with $\sigma_0 = \text{median}(\text{lower half of } s)$ as the noise-floor estimate. $\varepsilon$ is swept to cover the full CR range. | $n_c n_s / (r_\varepsilon(n_c+n_s))$ | ε ∈ logspace(10⁴, 10⁻¹, 30) |
| **WP** | Second-stage: db4 wavelet-packet adaptive thresholding on the $r$ temporal rows of $V_r^\top$. Per-component threshold $\tau_k = \alpha \sigma_0 / \sigma_k$ ensures uniform error contribution across all ranks. | $\text{CR}_\text{SVD} \times \text{CR}_\text{WP}$ | ε (SVD stage), α (WP stage) |

## Metrics

$$\text{RMSE}(c) = \left\langle \sqrt{\left\langle (x - \hat{x})^2 \right\rangle_t} \right\rangle_{\text{snippets}} \quad [\mu\text{V}] \qquad \text{SNR}(c) = 20 \cdot \log_{10} \left( \frac{\text{RMS}(c)}{\text{RMSE}(c)} \right) \quad [\text{dB}]$$

Aggregated as median over channels, then mean over 11 PIDs.

### Adaptive WP threshold calibration

After SVD truncation at rank $r$, each temporal component $V_k$ (a row of $V_r^\top$, unit-L2-norm) is wavelet-packet compressed with a per-component hard threshold:

$$\tau_k = \frac{\alpha \cdot \sigma_0}{\sigma_k}$$

where $\sigma_0$ is the same SVD noise floor used for ε-based rank selection, $\sigma_k$ is the singular value of component $k$, and $\alpha$ is a single global multiplier.
The threshold ensures every discarded coefficient contributes less than $\alpha \cdot \sigma_0$ — uniform across all components regardless of their amplitude.

- Dominant components (large $\sigma_k$) receive a small threshold → many WP coefficients retained.
- Weak components (small $\sigma_k$) receive a large threshold → only the coarsest WP structure kept.

**Choosing the operating point.** $\alpha$ and $\varepsilon$ are calibrated on the 11-PID benchmark (figure below): the recommended $\varepsilon \approx 150$, $\alpha \approx 28$ sits where CR is maximised while RMSE stays below ~25 µV, and the tight spread of the α-sweep curves across insertions confirms the pair generalises without per-recording tuning.

**Minimum retained coefficients (survival floor).** Because each $V_k$ has unit norm, its WP coefficients have a fixed magnitude ceiling ($\max_j|w_{kj}| \approx 0.2\text{–}0.4$). When even the *dominant* component is weak relative to the noise floor — $s_0/\sigma_0 \lesssim \alpha/\max_j|w_{0j}| \approx 140$ — the threshold $\tau_0$ exceeds every coefficient and the entire snippet is zeroed, silently discarding real low-amplitude LFP. A **survival floor** removes this failure mode: the dominant component ($k=0$) always keeps its $n_\text{min}=64$ largest-magnitude coefficients, so a retained chunk can never reconstruct to exact zero. Higher-SNR recordings are bit-for-bit unchanged (their dominant row already keeps far more than $n_\text{min}$), and saturation-muted spans — which enter the codec as all-zero — still reconstruct to zero regardless of the floor.

$$\text{CR}_\text{total} = \text{CR}_\text{SVD} \times \text{CR}_\text{WP}, \qquad \text{CR}_\text{WP} = \frac{r \cdot n_\text{WP\,slots}}{n_\text{kept}}$$

![α vs CR_WP for each SVD-stage CR (db4, level 5). Individual PIDs as thin lines; median as heavy line. Curves are tight across insertions, confirming α generalises across recordings.](figures/2026-06-12_svd_adaptive_wp_alpha_sweep.png)

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## SVD-adapt-WP algorithm in detail

The two-stage algorithm operates on a snippet matrix $X \in \mathbb{R}^{n_c \times n_s}$ (channels × samples):

**Stage 1 — spatial compression (SVD)**

$$X \approx \hat{X}_1 = U_r \, \text{diag}(s_r) \, V_r^\top$$

where $U_r \in \mathbb{R}^{n_c \times r}$, $s_r \in \mathbb{R}^r$, $V_r^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times n_s}$ are the top-$r$ singular triplets.
The rank $r$ is chosen to achieve a target CR (e.g. CR=24 → $r \approx 12$).

**Stage 2 — temporal compression (wavelet packets)**

Each of the $r$ rows of $V_r^\top$ is independently compressed using db4 wavelet packet decomposition (level 5).
Only the top-$f$ fraction of coefficients by magnitude are retained, giving an overall:

$$\text{CR}_{\text{total}} = \frac{n_c \, n_s}{r(n_c + n_s)} \cdot \frac{1}{f}$$

**SVD-adapt (ε-sweep)** selects rank automatically using:

$$\sigma_0 = \text{median}(s_{\lfloor r/2 \rfloor + 1}, \ldots, s_r), \qquad r^* = \max\{k : s_k > \varepsilon \cdot \sigma_0\}$$

Here $\sigma_0$ is the noise-floor estimate (median of the lower half of the full singular value spectrum), and $\varepsilon$ is a dimensionless threshold — the minimum signal-to-noise-floor ratio $s_k / \sigma_0$ required to retain a component. Equivalently, $\varepsilon(r) = s_r / \sigma_0$ is the $\varepsilon$ that would select exactly rank $r$ (as shown in the calibration figure). Sweeping $\varepsilon$ from $10^4$ (keep only the dominant component) down to $10^{-1}$ (keep almost everything) traces out the full CR curve.

**Reconstruction** reverses the two stages: reconstruct each wavelet-compressed row, then reassemble $\hat{X} = U_r \, \text{diag}(s_r) \, \hat{V}_r^\top$.
:::


::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## WP coefficient selection: per-coefficient error thresholding

**Setup.**
After SVD truncation at rank $r$, each retained temporal component is a row $V_k \in \mathbb{R}^{n_s}$ of $V_r^\top$ with unit $\ell_2$-norm ($\|V_k\|_2 = 1$, since $V$ is orthonormal).
The full reconstruction contribution of component $k$ to $X$ is $s_k U_k V_k^\top$, whose Frobenius norm is $s_k$.

**Wavelet-packet decomposition.**
Each $V_k$ is decomposed into $n_\text{WP}$ coefficients $\{w_{kj}\}$ via a full db4 wavelet-packet tree at level 5
(for $n_s = 750$, $n_\text{WP} = 960$).
Because the WP transform is orthogonal, $\sum_j w_{kj}^2 = \|V_k\|_2^2 = 1$.

**Per-component hard threshold.**
For each component $k$, a threshold is set as

$$\tau_k = \frac{\alpha \cdot \sigma_0}{s_k}$$

and coefficient $w_{kj}$ is retained only if $|w_{kj}| \geq \tau_k$; otherwise it is set to zero:

$$\tilde{w}_{kj} = w_{kj} \cdot \mathbf{1}\!\left[|w_{kj}| \geq \tau_k\right]$$

**Per-coefficient error guarantee.**
Zeroing $w_{kj}$ changes the reconstruction by $s_k \, U_k \cdot \delta v_{kj}^\top$, where $\delta v_{kj}$ is the inverse-WP basis vector for coefficient $j$ with unit norm.
The resulting Frobenius error contribution is

$$s_k \cdot |w_{kj}| \;<\; s_k \cdot \tau_k \;=\; \alpha \cdot \sigma_0$$

*Every discarded coefficient, in every component, contributes less than $\alpha \cdot \sigma_0$ to the reconstruction error* — uniformly across all ranks.
This is the same absolute noise-floor reference $\sigma_0$ used by the SVD stage, so the two thresholds speak the same language.

**Compression ratio.**
The WP stage CR is the ratio of total available coefficient slots to those retained:

$$\text{CR}_\text{WP} = \frac{r \cdot n_\text{WP}}{\#\{(k,j) : s_k |w_{kj}| \geq \alpha\sigma_0\}}$$

**Behaviour across the component spectrum.**

For a component with singular value $s_k = q \cdot \varepsilon \cdot \sigma_0$ (where $q \geq 1$, since only components above the SVD threshold are retained), the WP threshold becomes

$$\tau_k = \frac{\alpha}{q \cdot \varepsilon}$$

- **Dominant components** ($q \gg 1$, $s_k \gg \varepsilon\sigma_0$): $\tau_k$ is small, many WP coefficients survive — the component's full temporal structure is preserved with only fine-scale details discarded.
- **Marginal components** ($q \approx 1$, $s_k \approx \varepsilon\sigma_0$): $\tau_k \approx \alpha/\varepsilon$.  If $\alpha/\varepsilon$ exceeds the largest WP coefficient magnitude of $V_k$ (empirically 0.05–0.2 for LFP), the entire component is zeroed.  This is consistent behaviour: the component was weakly significant spatially *and* has no concentrated temporal structure, so it genuinely carries little information.

This component-level zeroing is not a design flaw — it is the natural outcome of applying a uniform per-coefficient error threshold to components with flat (noise-like) temporal spectra.
In practice, at the recommended operating point ($\varepsilon \approx 150$, $\alpha \approx 28$, $\alpha/\varepsilon \approx 0.19$), components at ranks 7–13 are fully eliminated by WP, while the first 5–6 components retain 5–70% of their WP coefficients for genuine temporal compression.

**Relationship to the SVD threshold.**
The two parameters are not independent: when $\alpha/\varepsilon > \max_j |w_{r,j}|$ (the largest WP coefficient of the weakest retained component), WP overrides the SVD rank selection.
The curves in the aggregate figure converge at high $\alpha$ because all $\varepsilon$ settings end up keeping the same dominant components once $\alpha$ is large enough to purge the weaker ones.
The non-redundant operating region is $\alpha/\varepsilon \lesssim 0.1$, where WP compresses temporal structure within every kept component without discarding any of them entirely.

**Survival floor on the dominant component.**
Purging *weak* components (above) is benign. The pathological case is when the same mechanism zeroes the *dominant* component $k=0$: this happens on low-SNR recordings where $s_0/\sigma_0 \lesssim \alpha/\max_j|w_{0j}| \approx 140$, at which point $\tau_0$ exceeds every coefficient of $V_0$, $\hat V_r^\top = 0$, and the chunk reconstructs to exact zero — destroying genuine low-amplitude LFP.
To bound this, the dominant component always retains its $n_\text{min}=64$ largest-magnitude WP coefficients regardless of $\tau_0$:
$$\#\{j : \tilde w_{0j} \neq 0\} \geq \min(n_\text{min},\, n_\text{WP}).$$
The floor is applied only to $k=0$, so weaker components still vanish (preserving CR), and it is a no-op on healthy recordings, whose dominant row already keeps $\gg n_\text{min}$ coefficients — leaving their reconstruction bit-for-bit identical. A genuinely silent input (e.g. a saturation-muted span) has $s_0 = 0$ hence $U_r\,\text{diag}(s_r) = 0$, so it still reconstructs to zero and the floor cannot fabricate signal.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Cadzow denoising with adaptive rank and imputation

**F-X Cadzow: working frequency bin by frequency bin** *(parameters used: nw=64, f_max=100 Hz, max rank r=5, gap_threshold=2.0, ppca_k=2.0)*

This is the *F-X* (frequency–space) variant of Cadzow denoising, borrowed from seismic processing.
Rather than applying SVD to the full time × channel matrix, the algorithm works one frequency bin at a time:

1. **rfft** the snippet → complex array $W \in \mathbb{C}^{n_c \times n_f}$.
2. For each frequency bin $f \leq f_\text{max}$, extract the spatial vector $w_f \in \mathbb{C}^{n_c}$ (one complex amplitude per channel).
3. Build a **block-Toeplitz trajectory matrix** $T_f$ from $w_f$.
4. Compute the rank-$r$ SVD of $T_f$, zero the remaining singular values, and read off the denoised amplitudes.
5. **irfft** back to the time domain.

**Outlier imputation (`ppca_k`)**: after the first rank-$r$ projection, channels deviating by more than $\text{median} + k \cdot \text{MAD}$ are replaced by their model prediction; the SVD is repeated on the cleaned data.
:::



::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Prior context: transform methods

Before focusing on SVD variants, we benchmarked six approaches: SVD, Wavelet Packets (WP), DCT, DCT-δ, STFT, and SVD+WP.
SVD consistently outperformed all transform-only methods at every compression ratio.
The figure below shows the full comparison; the current analysis refines and extends only the SVD family.

![Initial aggregate benchmark (11 PIDs) including all transform methods. SVD and SVD+WP dominate at every CR. DCT-δ is worst throughout.](figures/2026-06-06_compression_aggregate.png)

![Reconstruction gallery from initial benchmark — PID dab512bd. SVD retains spatial structure to CR=100; transform methods show block/stripe artefacts from CR=30.](figures/2026-06-06_compression_gallery_dab512bd-a02d-4c1f-8dbc-9155a163efc0.png)

![Residual gallery from initial benchmark. SVD/SVD+WP residuals are spatially incoherent; DCT and STFT residuals carry structured spectral artefacts at high CR.](figures/2026-06-06_compression_gallery_dab512bd-a02d-4c1f-8dbc-9155a163efc0_residual.png)
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="minimal"}
## Prior-context: Gap-criterion rank selection (discarded)

We investigated an alternative rank-selection criterion based on the largest relative drop in the singular value spectrum (the "gap"):

$$r_\text{gap} = \underset{i}{\arg\max}\; \frac{s_i}{s_{i+1}} + 1$$

We also swept a gap threshold $g$, defining rank as the last position where $s_k / s_{k+1} \geq g$.

![Gap ratio sv[k]/sv[k+1] at each rank boundary for each of the 11 PIDs. Reference lines at g=2, 5, 10.](figures/2026-06-10_gap_vs_rank.png)

The figure reveals why this criterion was discarded: after Cadzow denoising, the SV ratio at rank 1 is only **1.3–2.4** across all 11 PIDs — the dominant "gap" is barely larger than the secondary gaps.
There is no clean separation between signal and noise in the SV ratio spectrum, so the gap threshold has very little sensitivity to the compression ratio.
The ε-threshold (noise-floor-relative) criterion is far better calibrated for this data.
:::
